hypothesis: In a mid-market B2B sales organization, implementing a governed multi-agent sales operations system (for lead enrichment, routing, pipeline hygiene, and quote-to-order assistance) will reduce sales-ops/admin time per opportunity by at least 40% and average lead-response and quote cycle times by at least 20%, without degrading data quality or forecast accuracy relative to a well-instrumented manual baseline.

baseline.description: Current-state manual or semi-automated sales operations workflow in a sandbox or mirrored environment, with human sales operations staff and AEs handling lead enrichment, routing decisions, pipeline hygiene, and quote-to-order tasks using the existing CRM and tools.

process.lead_intake: Leads enter via existing channels (web forms, marketing automation, uploaded lists) and are pushed into the CRM as raw records without AI-driven augmentation.
process.enrichment: Sales operations or SDRs manually research each lead/account using the web, LinkedIn, enrichment tools (e.g., Clearbit/ZoomInfo), and internal notes, then copy/paste data into CRM fields.
process.routing: Leads/opportunities are routed to reps based on static rules (e.g., territory, segment) implemented via CRM assignment rules or manual reassignment by sales ops.
process.pipeline_hygiene: Sales managers and ops staff run regular pipeline reviews and manual clean-up (closing stale opportunities, fixing stages, updating amounts, next steps, close dates).
process.quote_to_order: AEs manually assemble quotes using CPQ tools or price books, obtain approvals by email/Slack, and create orders/contracts in CRM/CPQ/ERP, with little or no automation.
process.follow_ups: Task creation and follow-up cadences are driven by playbooks or human judgment, with reminders coming from basic CRM task functionality or email calendars.
process.forecasting_support: Sales leadership reviews pipeline reports and spreadsheets to estimate forecast; ops may lightly annotate or adjust, but no AI-driven assistance is used.

assignment.unit_of_randomization: Lead or opportunity record, depending on workflow being tested.
assignment.parallel_runs: For a given experimental window, incoming leads/opportunities are randomly assigned to baseline (manual) or treatment (agentic) paths while being handled by the same pool of reps and ops staff to control for skill differences.
assignment.human_role: In the baseline path, humans perform all enrichment, routing, hygiene, and quote tasks using their normal procedures; in the treatment path, they supervise or override agent suggestions where required by policy.

treatment.description: A coordinated multi-agent sales operations system integrated with the CRM and communication tools that automates lead enrichment, routing, pipeline hygiene prompts, and quote-to-order preparation under human supervision.

agents.name: Lead_Enrichment_Agent
agents.responsibility: Automatically enrich new leads and accounts with firmographic and contact data using external APIs and web search, and write structured values into CRM fields.
tools: CRM_API_Tool (read/write access to lead and account objects)
agents.human_approval: Enriched fields flagged for human review if confidence scores are below a configurable threshold or if overwriting non-empty high-trust fields.

agents.name: Lead_Routing_Agent
agents.responsibility: Assigns leads and opportunities to the correct owner based on territory, segment, product interest, and round-robin rules.
agents.human_approval: For ambiguous leads (e.g., multiple territory matches, high ARR potential), proposes assignee and awaits sales-ops approval before executing assignment.

agents.name: Pipeline_Hygiene_Agent
agents.responsibility: Monitors the pipeline for stale or inconsistent records (e.g., overdue close dates, contradictory stages/amounts, missing next steps) and proposes updates.
tools: CRM_API_Tool (query opportunities, update fields, create tasks)
agents.human_approval: Operates in suggestion mode only: creates CRM tasks/comments or sends hygiene recommendations that must be accepted by reps or managers to take effect in the experimental phase.

agents.name: Quote_Assistant_Agent
agents.responsibility: Given an approved opportunity and configured products/pricing rules, drafts quotes or order forms and routes them for approval.
agents.human_approval: All customer-facing quotes require AE and, for high-value or exception cases, sales management approval before being sent or logged as final.

agents.name: Followup_Cadence_Agent
agents.responsibility: Creates and updates follow-up tasks and email drafts based on engagement signals and pipeline stage.
tools: Email_Draft_Tool (draft only, no send in sandbox)
Engagement_Event_Store (synthetic signals from marketing automation or website tracking)
agents.human_approval: AEs must approve outbound drafts before they are sent using the real email system; in the experiment, sending may be simulated to avoid real customers.

agents.name: Forecast_Support_Agent
agents.responsibility: Analyzes pipeline changes and suggests adjustments or risk flags for the sales forecast.
agents.human_approval: Forecast outputs are advisory only; sales leadership retains final forecast ownership.

event_sources: Forecast snapshot time reached (e.g., daily at 18:00)
workflow_examples: Opportunity updated (stage, close date) -> Pipeline_Hygiene_Agent -> potential task creation
Quote requested -> Quote_Assistant_Agent -> approval workflow -> final quote draft

high_risk_actions: Sending external emails to real prospects/customers
Changing opportunity stage to Closed Won/Lost

approval_flows.email_send: Agent drafts email -> AE reviews in CRM/email UI -> AE edits/approves -> platform sends or logs synthetic sending.
approval_flows.quote_change: Agent drafts quote -> AE review -> if discount > X% or ARR > Y, manager approval required -> quote marked final.
approval_flows.stage_change: Agent suggests stage update -> rep must click 'accept' to apply.
approval_flows.owner_reassignment: Agent proposes new owner -> sales ops must approve in routing dashboard.

governance_and_approvals.audit_trail: All agent actions and suggestions recorded with timestamp, agent_id, input context hash, and human responder (accept/reject/edit); persisted in an agent_actions table or log index.

workloads.name: Lead_Enrichment_and_Routing
workloads.description: Evaluate manual vs. agentic enrichment and routing on newly created leads in the CRM.
workloads.population: Synthetic or sandbox leads generated to resemble a mid-market B2B SaaS funnel, including firm size, industry, geography, and product-interest fields.

input_generation.method: Synthetic data generator script that creates leads with varying completeness and quality, including noisy or ambiguous data (e.g., personal vs. corporate emails).
input_generation.volume: At least 1,000 leads for a statistically meaningful comparison; 50% randomly assigned to baseline, 50% to treatment.
input_generation.stratification: Stratify on region, company size, inbound vs. outbound source to ensure balanced distribution across baseline and treatment.

tasks_baseline: Human sales-ops or SDR enriches lead fields based on web/LinkedIn/enrichment tool, logs time spent, and manually assigns owner based on documented routing rules.
tasks_treatment: Lead_Enrichment_Agent and Lead_Routing_Agent automatically enrich and propose owner assignments; humans only review low-confidence or flagged cases per policy.
Humans can override any agent decisions and their actions are logged.

workloads.name: Pipeline_Hygiene
workloads.description: Evaluate how agentic assistance affects pipeline data cleanliness and the effort required to maintain it.
workloads.population: Existing opportunities in a sandbox CRM, seeded with synthetic or anonymized data reflecting multiple stages, ages, and value bands.

input_generation.method: Snapshot of CRM opportunities cloned into sandbox, with intentional injection of data quality issues (e.g., missing next steps, unrealistic close dates, inconsistent stages vs. close probability).
input_generation.volume: At least 1,000 opportunities, randomly assigned to baseline or treatment groups at the opportunity level.
input_generation.time_window: Monitor hygiene over 4–6 weeks to capture multiple sales cycles and hygiene passes.

tasks_baseline: Managers and ops staff perform weekly or biweekly pipeline reviews and manually clean up records following their current practices.
tasks_treatment: Pipeline_Hygiene_Agent scans and proposes updates, creates tasks for reps, and surfaces prioritized hygiene issues; reps and managers accept or reject suggestions.
Human time spent on hygiene tasks is logged for comparison.

workloads.name: Quote_to_Order_Assistance
workloads.description: Measure the impact of agentic support on the time and accuracy of preparing quotes and order forms.
workloads.population: Opportunities reaching a predefined stage (e.g., Proposal/Quote) within the experimental period.

input_generation.method: Use real historical configurations to generate synthetic quote requests in sandbox (e.g., combinations of products, tiers, contract lengths, and discounts).
input_generation.volume: At least 200 quote events, split between baseline and treatment.
input_generation.constraints: No real customer data used unless fully anonymized; all documents generated in sandbox.

tasks_baseline: AEs manually construct quotes in CPQ or CRM based on product catalog and pricing policies, request approvals via existing channels, and log final quotes.
tasks_treatment: Quote_Assistant_Agent generates initial quote drafts based on opportunity data and pricing rules; AEs and managers review, edit, and approve via the approval workflow.
Agent logs time-to-draft; humans log incremental time to finalize.

workloads.name: Followup_and_Cycle_Time
workloads.description: Evaluate whether agentic follow-up planning and nudges reduce lead-response and opportunity cycle times.
workloads.population: Subset of leads and opportunities already in the Lead_Enrichment_and_Routing and Pipeline_Hygiene workloads, with follow-up behaviors tracked.

input_generation.method: Simulate engagement events (email opens/clicks, website visits) using a generator that feeds into the marketing automation sandbox.
input_generation.volume: At least 500 leads and 500 opportunities with tracked interactions during the experimental window.
input_generation.covariates: Segment by channel, deal size, and territory to evaluate heterogeneous effects.

tasks_baseline: Reps rely on standard CRM reminders, their own workflows, or marketing automation programs for follow-ups.
No AI agent proposes follow-up schedules or drafts messages.
tasks_treatment: Followup_Cadence_Agent creates follow-up tasks and drafts messages according to playbooks; reps review and send (or in sandbox, simulate sending).
Time from events to follow-up and total AE task management time are recorded.

workloads.name: Forecasting_Support
workloads.description: Assess whether an advisory Forecast_Support_Agent can provide forecasts comparable in accuracy to manual-only forecasts while reducing human effort.
workloads.population: All open opportunities above a minimum value threshold during the experimental period.

input_generation.method: Use historical opportunity trajectories and outcomes (anonymized/synthetic) replayed over time into the sandbox CRM.
input_generation.period: Simulate or run for 1–3 fiscal quarters to compare predicted vs. actual outcomes.
input_generation.assignment: Same portfolio of opportunities, but alternate between manual-only forecast cycles and manual+agent advisory cycles week-by-week or region-by-region.

tasks_baseline: Sales leaders and ops produce weekly/biweekly forecasts manually from CRM reports and spreadsheets.
tasks_treatment: Forecast_Support_Agent produces a suggested forecast and risk annotations; humans adjust and finalize.
Time spent preparing forecasts is tracked.

randomization.method: Uniform random assignment at lead/opportunity level within defined strata (e.g., segment, region, ARR band) to baseline or treatment.
randomization.implementation: Randomization script or service that tags each new lead/opportunity with experiment_group ∈ {baseline, treatment} at creation time and routes it to the corresponding workflow.
randomization.verification: Regular checks (e.g., daily) to confirm balanced distributions of key attributes across groups.

blinding.operator_blinding: Where feasible, sales reps and ops are not explicitly told which records are in which group; they only see that some records come with AI suggestions. Full blinding may not be possible but awareness should be minimized to reduce behavior bias.
blinding.analyst_blinding: Analysts evaluating results should work from de-identified datasets where group labels are masked until metric computations and cleaning rules are finalized.

timeframe.ramp_up_period: 1–2 weeks to stabilize agent behavior and fix integration issues; data from this period is logged but excluded from primary analysis.
timeframe.measurement_period: At least 4–8 weeks for enrichment/routing/hygiene/quotes; longer (1–3 quarters) for forecast accuracy evaluations.

traffic_splits.default_split: 50% baseline / 50% treatment during main measurement period.
traffic_splits.staged_rollout: Optionally start at 10–20% treatment traffic and gradually increase to 50% as stability is confirmed.

environmental_controls.sandbox_isolation: Run in a sandbox or mirrored CRM environment using synthetic or anonymized data so that experimental writes do not affect live customers.
environmental_controls.policy_freeze: Freeze major sales process changes (e.g., compensation plans, routing rules) during the main measurement window or carefully log and control for them.
environmental_controls.training_and_docs: Provide both groups with equivalent non-agentic process training; additional training specific to interacting with the agents is documented and timestamped.

metrics.name: lead_enrichment_time_per_lead
metrics.description: Average human time spent enriching each lead (baseline: full manual; treatment: review/override time only).

metrics.name: routing_decision_time_per_lead
metrics.description: Elapsed time from lead creation in CRM to stable owner assignment.

metrics.name: lead_response_time
metrics.description: Elapsed time from lead creation to first outbound contact attempt logged (call, email, or task creation).

metrics.name: pipeline_hygiene_hours_per_week
metrics.description: Aggregate human hours spent on pipeline review and data clean-up activities per week.

metrics.name: pipeline_data_quality_score
metrics.description: Composite index combining completeness (required fields filled), consistency (fields align with rules), and freshness (no stale opportunities beyond thresholds).

metrics.name: quote_cycle_time
metrics.description: Elapsed time from quote request initiation to final approved quote ready to send to customer (or synthetic equivalent).

metrics.name: quote_error_rate
metrics.description: Percentage of quotes requiring correction due to pricing, configuration, or policy errors before approval.

metrics.name: admin_hours_per_opportunity
metrics.description: Total human non-selling time logged on an opportunity for enrichment, routing corrections, data updates, quote prep, and admin follow-ups.

metrics.name: opportunity_cycle_time
metrics.description: Elapsed time from opportunity creation to closure (Won or Lost).

metrics.name: forecast_absolute_error
metrics.description: Absolute difference between forecasted revenue for a period and actual realized revenue for the same period.

metrics.name: forecast_mape
metrics.description: Mean Absolute Percentage Error of forecasts compared to actuals.

metrics.name: agent_suggestion_acceptance_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of agent-suggested actions (updates, assignments, quotes, follow-ups) that are accepted without modification by humans.

metrics.name: agent_override_rate
metrics.description: Proportion of agent actions that are overridden or corrected by humans after execution.

metrics.name: user_trust_score
metrics.description: Average rating from periodic surveys of sales reps and ops staff on their trust in and perceived usefulness of the agents.

metrics.name: system_cost_per_record
metrics.description: Estimated compute + API cost per processed lead/opportunity in the treatment group (LLM calls, enrichment APIs, infra).

guardrails.description: Pipeline data quality in the treatment group must not materially degrade.
Error rate for quotes must not increase meaningfully under agent assistance.
Forecast accuracy should not be significantly worse with agent support.

secondary.description: Indicates that proposed actions are generally reasonable and trusted.
Operators report moderate or higher trust in agents.

secondary.threshold: Agentic incremental cost per record yields estimated ROI >= 2x when combined with labor savings.
secondary.description: Basic economic viability check combining system cost per record with observed admin-hours reduction and estimated labor costs.

failure_modes.name: data_quality_degradation
failure_modes.description: Agent updates or suggestions systematically introduce inaccurate or inconsistent data into CRM (e.g., wrong company sizes, misclassified industries, incorrect stages).
failure_modes.detection: Monitor pipeline_data_quality_score, agent_override_rate, and targeted audits of a random sample of records.
failure_modes.mitigation: Tighten schemas, add validation rules, increase confidence thresholds, move some actions from auto-execute to suggestion-only, retrain or refine prompts.

failure_modes.name: routing_bias_or_instability
failure_modes.description: Lead_Routing_Agent disproportionately routes high-value leads to certain reps or causes frequent reassignments.
failure_modes.detection: Analyze distribution of lead values and counts by rep across groups; monitor reassignment rates and complaints.
failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce round-robin fairness constraints, cap reassignments per record, require approvals for reassigning high-ARR opportunities.

failure_modes.name: agent_loops_or_duplicate_actions
failure_modes.description: Orchestration mistakes cause agents to repeatedly act on the same record (e.g., repeatedly suggesting the same hygiene fix).
failure_modes.detection: Monitor logs for repeated actions on identical records within short time windows; check for unusual spikes in agent calls.
failure_modes.mitigation: Introduce idempotency keys, action cool-down periods, and explicit state flags (e.g., hygiene_checked_at).

failure_modes.name: user_rejection_and_bypass
failure_modes.description: Sales reps and ops staff ignore or bypass agent suggestions, resulting in low adoption and biased metrics.
failure_modes.detection: Low agent_suggestion_acceptance_rate, low interaction counts, qualitative feedback from surveys and interviews.
failure_modes.mitigation: Refine UX, improve suggestion quality, incorporate user feedback loops, adjust incentives, provide training and quick explanations of agent suggestions.

failure_modes.name: forecast_overreliance
failure_modes.description: Leaders rely too heavily on Forecast_Support_Agent outputs, even if performance is not yet validated.
failure_modes.detection: Discrepancies between agent-advised forecasts and final human overrides; large forecast errors combined with low override activity.
failure_modes.mitigation: Clearly label forecasts as advisory, require explicit review steps, and only consider automation of forecast inputs after sufficient validation periods.

failure_modes.name: cost_overrun
failure_modes.description: LLM and enrichment API usage drives higher-than-expected operational costs per record.
failure_modes.detection: Monitor system_cost_per_record and total experiment cost against budgeted thresholds.
failure_modes.mitigation: Cache enrichment results, reduce unnecessary LLM calls, tune model sizes or sampling strategies, and narrow tool invocation scope.

failure_modes.name: security_or_privacy_misconfigurations
failure_modes.description: Agents gain more access than needed or data leaves the sandbox environment inadvertently.
failure_modes.detection: Access control and audit log reviews, penetration testing in sandbox, automated detection of cross-environment writes.
failure_modes.mitigation: Enforce least-privilege for agent credentials, network segmentation, data masking/anonymization, and routine security reviews.

systems.crm: Sandbox instance of a mainstream CRM (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot, Dynamics) with API access and the ability to define custom fields and workflows.
systems.marketing_automation: Sandbox environment for marketing automation or a synthetic engagement event generator integrated with CRM.
systems.communication_tools: Sandbox or test tenants for email and messaging (e.g., Office 365 test accounts, Slack dev workspace) for notifications and draft emails.
systems.agent_platform: Python-based or similar orchestration framework to host agents, with support for LLM tool invocation, queues, and logging (could use open-source agentic frameworks or custom code).
systems.datastore: Relational database or data warehouse (e.g., Postgres, BigQuery) for logging agent actions, metrics, and experiment assignments.
systems.monitoring: Dashboarding/BI tool (e.g., Metabase, Grafana, or CRM analytics) to visualize metrics and experiment results.

data.synthetic_or_anonymized_crm_export: Leads, accounts, contacts, opportunities, and historical quotes with all sensitive fields masked or synthetic data generated following realistic distributions.
data.product_and_pricing_catalog: Synthetic product list, SKUs, price tiers, discount rules, and approval thresholds.
data.routing_and_territory_rules: Explicit JSON/YAML configuration for current routing rules to be shared between baseline documentation and agent logic.
data.engagement_events: Synthetic email, website, and marketing interactions tied to leads and contacts.

models_and_apis.llm: Access to at least one modern LLM via API or on-prem deployment with support for tool use and structured outputs.
models_and_apis.enrichment: Real or mocked enrichment APIs; if real, restricted to synthetic or consented test domains.
models_and_apis.authentication: Service accounts or OAuth apps for CRM and communication tools with restricted permissions.

infrastructure.runtime: Containerized agent services (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes) or managed compute that can scale based on workload.
infrastructure.queues: Message queues (e.g., RabbitMQ, SQS, Pub/Sub) or CRM-native event hooks for event-driven orchestration.
infrastructure.secrets_management: Secure storage for API keys and credentials (e.g., Vault, parameter store).

run_instructions.title: Prepare Sandbox CRM and Synthetic Dataset
actions: Clone the production CRM schema into a sandbox environment (objects, fields, validation rules) without copying raw PII or commercial data.
Generate synthetic or anonymized leads, accounts, contacts, opportunities, and quote history that resemble a mid-market B2B SaaS pipeline.
Inject controlled data-quality issues (missing fields, stale opportunities) to test pipeline hygiene agents.
Configure product catalog, pricing, routing, and territory rules as structured configuration files (JSON/YAML) used by both baseline documentation and treatment agents.

run_instructions.title: Implement Experiment Assignment and Logging
actions: Create an experiment_assignments table keyed by record_id with fields: experiment_id, group (baseline/treatment), assigned_at, and stratification variables.
Implement a service or CRM trigger that, upon lead/opportunity creation, calls a randomization function and records the assignment.
Ensure that both baseline and treatment workflows log all relevant actions (manual or agentic) with timestamps, user/agent identifiers, and time_spent fields into an actions_log table.

run_instructions.title: Implement Baseline Time-Tracking Overlays
actions: Instrument baseline manual workflows with minimal friction time-tracking (e.g., browser plugin, simple timers inside CRM, or post-task self-report forms).
Pilot with a small group of reps and ops staff to calibrate and ensure consistent use; refine UI/UX to reduce under-reporting and fatigue.
Define clear guidelines on what constitutes 'admin work' vs. 'selling time' so participants log consistently.

run_instructions.title: Implement Multi-Agent Orchestration Layer
actions: Deploy an agent orchestration service that listens to CRM events via webhooks, polling, or message queues.

Implement each agent (Lead_Enrichment_Agent, Lead_Routing_Agent, Pipeline_Hygiene_Agent, Quote_Assistant_Agent, Followup_Cadence_Agent, Forecast_Support_Agent) as separate components with clear tool interfaces.
Connect agents to CRM, enrichment, pricing, and communication tools using scoped service accounts and enforce least-privilege access.
Implement robust logging in the agent layer, including input payloads (hashed or redacted), outputs, chosen tools, token usage, and any encountered errors.

run_instructions.title: Configure Human Approval and Guardrails
actions: Define policies for which actions require human approval vs. can be auto-executed, and translate them into agent and orchestrator configuration.
Integrate approval flows into CRM UIs or workflow tools so that reps and managers can accept/decline agent suggestions with minimal friction.
Add explicit labels and explanations to agent suggestions so humans understand what the agent is proposing and why.

Verify that all high-risk actions (e.g., quote finalization, external communications, stage changes to Closed Won/Lost) cannot occur without appropriate approval in both baseline and treatment groups.

run_instructions.title: Conduct Ramp-Up and Sanity Checks
actions: Run agents in shadow mode on a subset of records (e.g., 10–20% traffic) while humans still perform full manual tasks; log agent outputs and compare with human decisions without acting on them.
Audit a random sample of agent suggestions for accuracy and policy conformance; fix prompt templates, rules, and tool configurations as needed.
Once performance is acceptable, enable agents to perform suggestion-mode actions in treatment group; gradually enable auto-execution for low-risk actions where appropriate.

run_instructions.title: Run Main Experiment
actions: Activate full 50/50 baseline/treatment traffic split for the defined measurement period.
Monitor operational dashboards daily for anomalies in key metrics (e.g., quote errors, data quality, system errors, override rates).
Collect weekly qualitative feedback from a sample of reps and ops staff regarding agent usability and trust.
Avoid introducing major process or compensation changes during the period; if unavoidable, document changes with timestamps for later analysis.

run_instructions.title: Compute Metrics and Analyze Results
actions: Extract experiment data into an analysis environment, joining CRM data, experiment_assignments, and actions_log tables.

Compute per-record metrics (e.g., admin_hours_per_opportunity, lead_response_time, quote_cycle_time) and aggregate/week-level metrics (e.g., pipeline_hygiene_hours_per_week, pipeline_data_quality_score).
Perform statistical tests specified in success_criteria to assess differences between baseline and treatment groups.
Segment results by region, deal size, and channel to identify subpopulations where the agentic system performs particularly well or poorly.

run_instructions.title: Review Experimental Results and Refine Agent Design
actions: Compare observed metrics against success and guardrail thresholds; identify trade-offs (e.g., time savings vs. small accuracy changes).
Examine failure modes (e.g., cases with high override rates or errors) and trace back to specific prompts, tools, or workflows.
Iteratively refine agent prompts, rules, and approval thresholds, then re-run smaller targeted experiments or canary rollouts to validate improvements.
Document lessons learned and adaptation guidelines so readers can replicate, adapt, or extend these patterns to their own sales stacks and processes.

derived_metrics.name: admin_hours_per_opportunity
derived_metrics.definition: For each opportunity, sum duration_seconds for actions where actor_type = 'human' and action_type in {enrichment, routing, hygiene_update, quote_prep, admin_task}, then divide by 3600.

derived_metrics.name: lead_response_time
derived_metrics.definition: For each lead, time difference between event_type='lead_created' and first event_type in {'outbound_email_sent', 'call_logged', 'task_created_for_followup'}.

derived_metrics.name: pipeline_data_quality_score
derived_metrics.definition: Weighted average of data_completeness_score, data_consistency_score, and data_freshness_score for all open opportunities at regular snapshot times.

derived_metrics.name: quote_cycle_time
derived_metrics.definition: For each quote, difference between event_type='quote_requested' and event_type='quote_final_approved'.

derived_metrics.name: quote_error_rate
derived_metrics.definition: Number of quotes with at least one action_type='quote_correction' divided by total quotes in group.

derived_metrics.name: forecast_mape
derived_metrics.definition: Mean over periods of |forecast_value - actual_value| / max(actual_value, epsilon), expressed as a percentage.

derived_metrics.name: system_cost_per_record
derived_metrics.definition: Total api_cost for agent actions in treatment group divided by the number of unique leads/opportunities processed in that group.

required_plots: Distribution plots (histograms/boxplots) of admin_hours_per_opportunity for baseline vs. treatment.
Kaplan-Meier or cumulative density plots of lead_response_time and quote_cycle_time for both groups.
Time series of pipeline_data_quality_score over the experiment period for baseline and treatment.
Bar charts of forecast_absolute_error and forecast_mape per period by group.
Stacked bar or heatmaps of agent_suggestion_acceptance_rate and agent_override_rate by agent type.
required_tables: Summary table of all primary and guardrail metrics with baseline mean/median, treatment mean/median, absolute and relative differences, and p-values.
Segmented results by region, deal size, and channel for key metrics.
Catalog of identified failure modes with example records, root-cause analysis, and mitigation steps taken.
